title: Every field extension is a directed union of global complete intersection subalgebras
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $K/k$ a field extension [def-pc-field-extension]. Then for every finite subset $E\subseteq K$ there are integers $n,c\ge0$, elements $f_1,\dots,f_c$ of the polynomial ring $k[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-mv-polynomial-ring] which form a regular sequence in $k[X_1,\dots,X_n]$ [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence] (for $c=0$ the empty sequence), and an injective homomorphism of $k$-algebras $\iota:k[X_1,\dots,X_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)\to K$ whose image contains $E$. (This is the assertion that $K$ is the filtered colimit, here the directed union, of its $k$-subalgebras that are global complete intersections over $k$.)

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 07BV (lemma-colimit-syntomic, line 44527), first assertion, in the form its proof (lines 44535-44559) reduces it to: for a finite subset E there is a k-subalgebra A of K containing E with A = k[x_1,...,x_d,1/h,Y_1,...,Y_r]/(P_1,...,P_r), P_1,...,P_r a regular sequence; presented as k[x_1,...,x_d,T,Y_1,...,Y_r]/(hT-1,P_1,...,P_r) (hT-1 is a nonzerodivisor of the domain k[x,T,Y] with quotient k[x,1/h,Y]), so n = d+1+r, c = r+1. Tag verified in literature/stacks-project/tags/tags (07BV,algebra-lemma-colimit-syntomic).

proof.text: Fix a finite subset $E\subseteq K$ and let $L=k(E)\subseteq K$ be the subfield generated by $k$ and the elements of $E$ [def-weil-pbc-transcendence-basis]. It is a finitely generated field extension of $k$. By [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-finite-transcendence-basis], choose a finite transcendence basis $x_1,\dots,x_d$ of $L/k$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07BV (lemma-colimit-syntomic), lines 44535-44541: subfield generated by E and a finite transcendence basis

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-finitely-generated-field-complete-intersection-model] to $L/k$ and the basis from step 1. It gives a nonzero domain $A=k[X_1,\dots,X_n]/(f_1,\dots,f_c)$ with $f_1,\dots,f_c$ a regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence], together with an injective $k$-algebra homomorphism $A\to L$ inducing $\operatorname{Frac}(A)\cong L$. Identify $A$ with its image in $L$.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07BV (lemma-colimit-syntomic), lines 44541-44554: the tower of monic minimal polynomials and its regular-sequence presentation

proof.text: For the finite subset in L=k(E), apply the proved private exists_common_denominator lemma. Induct on the Finset: use denominator 1 for the empty set; adding z=a/s to a set with common denominator g replaces the denominator by sg and adjusts the old and new numerators. Injectivity into L ensures the images of nonzero s and g remain nonzero, so field_simp verifies both identities. Lift the embedding to A[1/g] by IsLocalization.Away.liftAlgHom; injective_iff_map_algebraMap_eq and the original embedding show the lift is injective.

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 07BV (lemma-colimit-syntomic), lines 44554-44559: enlarge h to put E in A; Algebra, proof of Lemma Tag 00SA (lemma-localize-lci), lines 35868-35881

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-sequence-quotient-localization-presentation] to the regular-sequence domain model A and the nonzero common denominator g. It supplies a regular sequence q of length f.length+1 and a k-algebra equivalence from its polynomial quotient to A[1/g]. Compose this equivalence, the localization embedding into L, and L.val into K. Each composite is injective. For x in E with x=a/g, take the inverse image under the equivalence of the localization element a times invSelf(g); map_mul and mul_invSelf verify that it maps to x.

split_report.summary: Split Stacks 07BV into five steps using the existing finite-transcendence-basis and finitely-generated-field complete-intersection-model nodes: form L=k(E), obtain a regular-sequence domain model A with fraction field L, clear the finitely many denominators by one principal localization A_g, present A_g as k[X,T]/(f,hT-1), check the entire displayed sequence is regular and the quotient nonzero, then derive directedness from finite generation. The imported statement was kept. The existing principal-localization global-complete-intersection node was not used because its dimension-based conclusion does not itself assert the explicit regular-sequence presentation required here.
